_readme: HOW TO EDIT: each course needs id, name, description, riasec (all six keys, 0-10),
subjects (secondary tags, must match tags used in questions.json), and scoringNote.
Add or remove courses freely - the app reads whatever is in this list.
Scores are RELATIVE SHAPE, not quality. Cosine similarity ignores overall magnitude,
so what matters is which dimensions are high compared to the others in the SAME course.

courses.name: BS Civil Engineering
courses.description: Design, analyze, and supervise the construction of roads, bridges, buildings, and water systems.
courses.scoringNote: R and I lead: physical structures built from heavy analysis. C is high because codes, specs, and tolerances are non-negotiable. Low A/S - little design expression or direct people work.

courses.name: BS Computer Science
courses.description: Study algorithms, data structures, and software systems, and build programs that solve real problems.
courses.scoringNote: I dominates: the work is abstract problem-solving. C is high for precision and structure, R moderate for hands-on building. A moderate - there is real design taste in software. S is lowest.

courses.name: BS Architecture
courses.description: Design buildings and spaces that balance how they look, how they are used, and how they get built.
courses.scoringNote: A leads - this is a design discipline first. R and C follow because drawings must survive contact with structure, budget, and building code. E moderate for client work.

courses.name: BS Nursing
courses.description: Train in clinical care, assessment, and patient management across hospital and community settings.
courses.scoringNote: S is the highest of any course here - the job is people, continuously. C is high for charting and protocol, R and I moderate for hands-on procedures and clinical reasoning.

courses.name: BS Biology
courses.description: Study living systems from cells to ecosystems, with heavy laboratory and field work.
courses.scoringNote: Purest I profile in the list - investigation is the entire point. R and C moderate for lab technique and meticulous protocol. E is lowest; this is not a persuasion field.

courses.name: BS Psychology
courses.description: Study human behavior and mental processes using research methods, assessment, and counseling foundations.
courses.scoringNote: S and I together - it is a people-facing field built on research method and statistics. A moderate for interpretation and writing. R is lowest; almost nothing is physical.

courses.name: BS Accountancy
courses.description: Master financial reporting, auditing, and taxation, with strong emphasis on standards and controls.
courses.scoringNote: Highest C in the list - the work is rules, records, and accuracy. E moderate for advisory and client-facing roles. A is the lowest score anywhere; improvisation is a liability here.

courses.name: BSBA - Marketing Management
courses.description: Learn how products find their audience: consumer behavior, branding, campaigns, and sales strategy.
courses.scoringNote: E leads - persuasion and initiative drive the field. A high for campaign and brand work, S high because it is fundamentally about reading people. R lowest.

courses.name: BA Communication
courses.description: Study media, journalism, and public communication, and practice producing content across formats.
courses.scoringNote: A leads on the production and storytelling side, with S and E close behind since the output is aimed at an audience. I moderate for research and reporting.

courses.name: BFA Multimedia Arts
courses.description: Build a practice in visual design, illustration, animation, and motion across digital media.
courses.scoringNote: The most A-dominant course here, with everything else deliberately low. R moderate because the tools are technical and hands-on.

courses.name: Bachelor of Secondary Education
courses.description: Prepare to teach a major subject in high school, covering pedagogy, assessment, and classroom practice.
courses.scoringNote: S at the ceiling - the work is sustained human contact. A and E moderate-high because explaining well is a performance. I moderate for subject mastery.

courses.name: BS Hospitality Management
courses.description: Run hotels, restaurants, and events: service operations, food and beverage, and guest experience.
courses.scoringNote: S and E lead - service plus commercial pressure. C and R follow for operations, standards, and genuinely physical shift work. I is lowest; little research involved.
